title: Samantha's ₹100 Crore Blockbuster Hits JioHotstar This Thursday. She Shot Part of It With Morning Sickness.
excerpt: Maa Inti Bangaaram is the highest-grossing solo female-led Telugu film ever. Now the pregnant star — who also produced it with husband Raj Nidimoru — is taking a maternity break on the biggest high of her career.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Samantha's *Maa Inti Bangaaram* grossed over ₹100 crore, a record for solo female-led Telugu films.
  • The film premieres on JioHotstar on July 17, 2026, just weeks after its theatrical release.
  • Samantha filmed while pregnant, battling morning sickness during production's final stretch.
  • Raj Nidimoru praised the film's success, stating it received more appreciation than his previous hits.
  • Samantha plans to take maternity leave after this film, expecting her first child in December 2026.

The numbers landed first. Then the news that made them feel small. https://youtube.com/watch?v=B9d-wISnm8s **Samantha Ruth Prabhu**'s *Maa Inti Bangaaram* has officially crossed **₹100 crore worldwide** — making it the highest-grossing solo female-led Telugu film in history, surpassing *Rudhramadevi* and rewriting what's commercially possible when a woman carries the entire film on her back. And starting **July 17**, the whole thing lands on **JioHotstar**, giving the global diaspora its first chance to see what all of India has been talking about for the past month. But here's the part that makes the hundred-crore number feel like a footnote. ## She Was Pregnant the Entire Time At the film's success meet in Hyderabad — with her husband and the film's creator **Raj Nidimoru** seated beside her — a visibly glowing Samantha confirmed what fans had been speculating for weeks. She's expecting her first child, due **December 2026**. > "After Maa Inti Bangaaram, I will have to take a small gap, given my condition. I'll have to take maternity leave. But I am very, very happy, and after that, I'll be back with another film for my fans." — Samantha Ruth Prabhu > **"So it is very special." — Raj Nidimoru He also let slip something more personal: "Samantha never wanted to make more films, but I asked her to do one more." That "one more" just crossed ₹100 crore."** Director **B. V. Nandini Reddy** later revealed that Samantha had been in her first trimester during the film's final stretch of production. When it came time to shoot the high-energy Thassadiya song — a fast-paced, physically demanding wedding number — the actress was battling severe morning sickness. "I was very happy. It was almost towards the end of the shoot," Nandini said. "They first told me that she wasn't feeling well in the morning. We thought she must have a fever. The next day I asked her if her fever had come down. At first, she didn't say anything. A minute later, she said, actually, I'm carrying and suffering from morning sickness." The action sequences, mercifully, had already been filmed. But the fact that she powered through those musical sequences while growing a human being inside her? That's not grit. That's something closer to mythology. ![Raj Nidimoru — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d7/Raj_%26_DK.jpg/3840px-Raj_%26_DK.jpg) ## The Film That Raj Nidimoru Says Hit Harder Than *Stree* and *The Family Man* *Maa Inti Bangaaram* (translated: "The Gold of Our Home") follows **Swarna**, an orphan who elopes with Dr. Anirudh (**Diganth Manchale**) and returns to his traditional, patriarchal village household for a family wedding. She plays the docile, obedient daughter-in-law to perfection — because she has to. Her real name is **Jhansi**, a deadly former assassin and ex-Naxalite rebel, and the domestic bliss is a cover. When her obsessive former gang leader **Karuna** (**Gulshan Devaiah**, chilling and magnetic) tracks her down, the saree-clad bride picks up the gun again to defend the very in-laws who doubted her. It's the kind of premise that sounds like a pitch meeting fever dream — *Dangal* meets *Kill Bill* meets a Telugu family drama — but under Nandini Reddy's direction and Raj Nidimoru's razor-sharp script, it works. Brilliantly. **Santhosh Narayanan**'s score shifts between warmth and menace like a knife hidden in a bouquet. At the film's success celebrations, Raj — who also co-produced the film alongside Samantha under their **Tralala Moving Pictures** banner — made a startling admission.
Samantha's Journey
›Filmed during pregnancy, facing morning sickness.
›Confirmed pregnancy at film's success meet.
›Plans maternity leave after the film's release.
›Due date for first child: December 2026.
> "We did so much in Hindi. The Family Man and Stree came and became blockbusters, but I got greater appreciation for Maa Inti Bangaaram than I did for them. So it is very special." — Raj Nidimoru He also let slip something more personal: "Samantha never wanted to make more films, but I asked her to do one more." That "one more" just crossed ₹100 crore. ## What the Diaspora Needs to Know *Maa Inti Bangaaram* premieres on **JioHotstar** on **Thursday, July 17, 2026** — less than four weeks after its theatrical release on June 19. It opened to a ₹50 crore worldwide weekend, built steadily through word-of-mouth, and has now held theatres for nearly a month on raw audience love. The film is in **Telugu**, with a Tamil-dubbed version released theatrically as *Engal Thangam*. Expect JioHotstar to offer it with subtitles for the wider South Asian diaspora. For NRIs who missed the theatrical run — and for anyone who watched Samantha battle autoimmune disease rumours, a public divorce, and tabloid speculation over the past few years — this film is the answer to every question about whether she still has it. She has it. She never lost it.
Director's Praise
›Raj Nidimoru claims greater appreciation for this film than for *The Family Man* and *Stree*.
›Samantha initially hesitant to make more films.
›Raj encouraged her to take on this project.
And now she's taking a break. Going to have a baby. Going to come back. Mark July 17 on the calendar.
